reproduction_target: Comparative-genomics and sequence-structure survey of BacteRiophage EXclusion (BREX) systems and newly proposed BREX-related (BR) systems. Computational target: (i) recover the full phyletic spread of BREX/BR systems by iterative profile searches anchored on BrxC-ATPase and PglZ against the NCBI nr database (PSI-BLAST, JACKHMMER, HMMSCAN/HMMSEARCH, BLASTP, RPS-BLAST, HHpred/HHblits); (ii) cluster and de-duplicate hits (BLASTCLUST, CD-HIT) and build representative multiple sequence alignments (MAFFT, Kalign v3, GISMO) with manual refinement; (iii) predict and compare 3D structures (AlphaFold3, DALI, Foldseek, JPred v4, PyMOL) to assign domain-level annotations; (iv) reconstruct gene neighbourhoods with an in-house Perl script over GenBank assemblies and assign taxonomy from NCBI Taxonomy; (v) infer phylogenies (FastTree, IQ-TREE) and render trees (FigTree); (vi) compute position-wise Shannon entropy per alignment column and visualise in R. The paper contains no wet-lab experiments, so W = 0.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation list built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML 'Materials and Methods' section (retrieved by curl from the .source.xml endpoint; title string verified present in the fetched file). No workflow file exists anywhere - the paper deposits no code at all, so there is no Snakefile/Nextflow/Makefile to anchor granularity on. Web-server invocations (HHpred, DALI, Foldseek, AlphaFold3, JPred) are counted as steps because they are named tool invocations that produce the paper's primary evidence. Manual alignment refinement is counted as a step because the Methods explicitly make it part of the pipeline ('The resulting alignments were manually refined...'), and it is the point where the analysis becomes irreproducible in principle. Stage-1 read only; no code was executed and no source was read line-by-line.

steps.label: Iterative PSI-BLAST profile searches against the NCBI non-redundant (nr) protein database, anchored on BrxC-ATPase and PglZ; PSSMs regenerated and refined at each iteration until convergence or false-positive onset (RRID:SCR_001010)
Iterative JACKHMMER HMM-profile searches against NCBI nr, seeded from the same anchor proteins; HMM profiles refined at each step (RRID:SCR_005305)
Sensitive HMM profile-profile homology verification with the online HHpred server against the PDB (RRID:SCR_012820) and Pfam databases (RRID:SCR_010276)
Generation of the multiple sequence alignments consumed by HHpred, using HHblits against the UniRef30 database with default parameters
Reciprocal BLASTP searches against NCBI nr for borderline-score distant homologs recovered in the initial iterative searches (RRID:SCR_001010)
Local RPS-BLAST searches against the Pfam database and against 'a custom in-house profile database containing a diverse range of protein domains' (the in-house database is not deposited or described)

Clustering of all retrieved homologous sequences with BLASTCLUST version 2.2.26 (RRID:SCR_016641), minimum alignment coverage L = 0.2-0.5 and bit-score threshold S = 20-50, 'manually optimized' per cluster
Redundancy reduction within each cluster using CD-HIT (RRID:SCR_007105) with sequence identity -c 0.4-0.9 and word length -n 2-5, 'adjusted as needed'
Representative MSA construction with MAFFT using the local-pair algorithm and --maxiterate 1000 (RRID:SCR_011811)
Representative MSA construction with Kalign V3 using default parameters (RRID:SCR_011810)
Representative MSA construction with GISMO using the -fast parameter

Manual refinement of all resulting alignments using profile-search information, predicted 3D models, structural alignments and secondary-structure predictions (human curation step, no protocol or decision rules recorded)
3D structural model prediction with AlphaFold3 (AF3) from the representative MSAs (RRID:SCR_025885); no seed, model preset, MSA-mode, recycle count or run date reported
Structural similarity search of each AF3 model with the DALI server against the PDB clustered at 50-75% sequence identity, homology inferred at Z-score >= 4 (RRID:SCR_013433)
Structural similarity search with the FOLDSEEK server against AlphaFoldDB UniProt50 and the PDB at 100% identity (no E-value, sensitivity or alignment-mode reported)
Secondary-structure prediction for all MSAs with JPred v4 (RRID:SCR_016504)
Visualisation and rendering of the fully annotated 3D models (domain architecture + secondary structure) in PyMOL (RRID:SCR_000305, https://www.pymol.org/)

Gene-neighbourhood extraction with 'an in-house Perl script' that parses GenBank genome files keyed by GCA assembly IDs to pull upstream/downstream genes flanking each query; inclusion filters were adjacent-gene spacing <= ~100 nt, conserved gene orientation, and recurrence across multiple phyla. The script is not deposited.

Re-clustering of neighbourhood protein products with BLASTCLUST, per-cluster annotation through the sequence-structure pipeline, and merge/split decisions for small divergent clusters and singlets based on 'shared sequence motifs or structural synapomorphies' (curator judgement, no rule set given)
Taxonomic distribution assignment for all analysed protein sequences using the NCBI Taxonomy Database (no snapshot date, dump version or mapping procedure reported)
Approximate maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference with FastTree (RRID:SCR_015501) using -spr 4, -mlacc and -slownni; local support values estimated by the program default

Complementary maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference with IQ-TREE (RRID:SCR_017254) under an 'edge-linked partition model' with ultrafast bootstrap, 1000 replicates; partition definitions, substitution models and random seed are not reported
Final tree visualisation and rendering with FigTree (RRID:SCR_008515, https://tree.bio.ed.ac.uk/software/figtree/)

Position-wise Shannon entropy per MSA column (formula given in the Methods; range 0 to 4.32) computed, analysed and visualised 'using the R programming language'; no script, package, R version or plotting code is deposited

headline.static_readiness: 0/24 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted; declared environment statically valid but not verified as the env that produced the results. n_exact_capture_unexecuted=0, n_fetch_required=0. Under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 2/24 (8%) readiness upper bound (R-star + RI), stage-1 prose ceiling; never 'reproducible'. Only C7 (BLASTCLUST 2.2.26) and C10 (Kalign V3, default parameters) reach every axis >= 1, because they are the only two steps where a version string and a usable parameter statement coexist. The remaining 22/24 steps cap at NI, driven by three distinct causes: (a) version silence - 19 of the 24 steps score version=0, covering PSI-BLAST, JACKHMMER, HHpred, HHblits, BLASTP, RPS-BLAST, HMMSCAN/HMMSEARCH, CD-HIT, MAFFT, GISMO, DALI, Foldseek, PyMOL, FastTree, IQ-TREE, FigTree and R, most of which carry an RRID but no version, and an RRID identifies the tool, not the build; (b) unpublished code and data - the custom in-house RPS-BLAST profile database (C6) and the in-house Perl gene-neighbourhood script (C18) are named but never deposited, and no code repository exists for the paper at all; (c) parameter silence at the search layer - the iterative PSI-BLAST/JACKHMMER/HHpred/BLASTP searches that define the entire sequence set report no E-value cut-off, iteration count or convergence criterion, so the primary dataset cannot be regenerated. Two further structural limits sit above the axis scores: the manual alignment refinement and manual cluster merge/split decisions (C12, C19) are irreducibly human, and every profile search targets NCBI nr / PDB / Pfam / UniRef30 / AlphaFoldDB at an unstated access date, so even a perfect re-run would query a different database. No step could exceed RI even under stage-2 execution, because no lockfile, conda specification, container digest or release snapshot is claimed anywhere in the paper.
headline.coverage: 24 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS 'Materials and Methods' section. 0 wet-lab steps: the study is entirely comparative genomics and sequence-structure analysis, with no experimental work. Coverage = 24/24 (100%) of enumerated steps; computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 100%.

gaps.where: Whole paper - there is no 'Code availability' section. The only availability statement is 'Data availability', which points at supplementary files and a Zenodo dataset deposit.
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked anywhere: no GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repository, no Software Heritage archive, no code Zenodo DOI. The Zenodo record cited (10.5281/zenodo.17293984) is registered as resource type 'Dataset' and contains a single supplementary-data ZIP, not software.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the driver scripts, the in-house Perl neighbourhood extractor, the entropy/R plotting code and the search/cluster wrapper commands in a public repository, tag a release, archive it to Zenodo with a software DOI, and add a Code availability statement citing that DOI.

gaps.missing: Two named in-house artifacts are never released: (i) 'a custom in-house profile database containing a diverse range of protein domains' used for local RPS-BLAST searches - no size, composition, construction procedure or download is given; (ii) 'an in-house Perl script designed to extract upstream and downstream genes flanking the query gene of interest' - no source, no parameters beyond the ~100 nt adjacency rule. Both sit on the critical path: the custom profile DB drives domain annotation and the Perl script produces every genomic-neighbourhood figure.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the custom profile database (or its build recipe plus the source profiles) and the Perl script under version control, and cite them from a Code availability statement.

gaps.missing: Version records are almost entirely absent. Only BLASTCLUST carries an exact pin (2.2.26); Kalign V3, JPred v4 and AlphaFold3 give a major version only. PSI-BLAST, JACKHMMER, HHpred, HHblits, BLASTP, RPS-BLAST, HMMSCAN/HMMSEARCH, CD-HIT, MAFFT, GISMO, DALI, Foldseek, PyMOL, FastTree, IQ-TREE, FigTree and R are named with an RRID but no version at all. RRIDs identify a tool, not a build, and cannot substitute for a version pin.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version (and for web servers, the server release plus access date) of every tool used, and ship a conda-lock / pixi lockfile or a container image digest covering the locally-run stack.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C14, C15, C18, C20 - every external reference resource
gaps.missing: No reference database is pinned or dated: NCBI nr, Pfam, PDB, UniRef30, AlphaFoldDB UniProt50, the GenBank assembly set behind the GCA-keyed neighbourhood extraction, and the NCBI Taxonomy Database are all consumed at an unstated release. These are rolling resources; nr in particular grows daily. Because the search phase defines the sequence set that every downstream step consumes, an unpinned nr poisons the entire pipeline. No workflow exists in which the pin could live, so this is prose-level absence rather than class B.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the release/version and access date of each database (nr download date, Pfam release number, PDB snapshot, UniRef30 release, AlphaFoldDB version, NCBI Taxonomy dump date) and, preferably, deposit the exact FASTA/profile snapshots used.

gaps.where: C12 (manual alignment refinement), C19 (cluster merge/split decisions), and the 'Systematic Curation of BrxC and PglZ Homologs' multi-step screening described in Results
gaps.missing: Core decisions are made by human curation with no recorded rule set: alignments are 'manually refined using information from profile-based searches, predicted 3D structural models, structural alignments, and secondary structure predictions'; small divergent clusters and singlets are 'either merged with existing clusters or retained as distinct groups' based on 'shared sequence motifs or structural synapomorphies'; BLASTCLUST L/S and CD-HIT -c/-n are 'manually optimized' / 'adjusted as needed' per cluster with only ranges reported. The exact per-cluster values are unrecoverable.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the per-cluster parameter table actually used, and either encode the merge/split criteria as a scripted rule or release the intermediate and final alignment/cluster files at every curation checkpoint so downstream users can start from the curated state.

gaps.where: C13 (AlphaFold3), C21 (FastTree -spr 4 / -mlacc / -slownni), C22 (IQ-TREE ultrafast bootstrap x1000)
gaps.missing: Three stochastic steps report no random seed. AlphaFold3 additionally omits the model preset, MSA mode, recycle count and inference date; IQ-TREE omits the partition definitions and substitution models under its 'edge-linked partition model'. Reruns can therefore only be compared distributionally, not exactly.
gaps.how_to_close: Report seeds and, for AF3, the exact model/preset and inference date; for IQ-TREE, publish the partition file and the selected substitution models; deposit the resulting trees in Newick form alongside the alignments.

gaps.where: C3 (HHpred), C13 (AlphaFold3), C14 (DALI server), C15 (FOLDSEEK server), C16 (JPred v4)
gaps.missing: Five substantive analysis steps are externalised to web servers whose code, backing database snapshot and default settings change over time and are not under the authors' control. No access dates or server versions are given, so these steps cannot be re-executed against the same state.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the access date and server version for each web service, and deposit the raw server outputs (HHpred result files, AF3 CIF models with their confidence metrics, DALI and Foldseek hit tables, JPred predictions) so downstream users can start from the recorded results.

gaps.missing: The Methods link https://www.pymol.org/ (the Schrodinger commercial distribution) rather than the open-source build, and give no version. Figure rendering is therefore nominally dependent on a licensed product at an unknown version. Impact is limited to figure production, not to the analytical conclusions.
gaps.how_to_close: State the PyMOL edition and version used, or note that open-source PyMOL reproduces the rendering, and deposit the .pse sessions or rendering scripts.
